author: Huang Yinzhou et al.
asr_identification: Bazhou No. 2 city 巴州二號古城, W of Guazhou county, 40°28′19″ N, 95°28′06″ E (printed 42°, a misprint: the stated 14 km from Liugong holds only at 40°)
evidence: Satellite imagery and fieldwork; 14 km NW of Liugong city (Tang Changle) for P.2005's 27 li 200 bu, and c. 14 km ENE of Xishawo No. 3 city (the Gancao post), on the Shazhou–Yizhou road.
quote: 巴州二号古城的具体位置为北纬42°28＇19＂，东经95°28＇6＂
note: differs from Li Zhengyu's site N of Liugong (14.6 km apart); the bearing 'NW' is Yan Gengwang's, not P.2005's

author: Huang Yinzhou et al.
evidence: The distance from Changle: Yan Gengwang's 'NW 27 li 200 bu' from Changle, measured on the ground.
quote: 二者实测直线距离接近14千米
note: 27.7 li = 14 km is 0.51 km per li; Changle–Jieting on the same paper's figures is 0.44

author: Huang Yinzhou et al.
evidence: The older view put the Xinjing post at the Leidunzi beacon N of the Great Wall W of the county; Huang dates Leidunzi to the Qing from its good preservation and its position due N of the Qing Baiqi bao.
quote: 这表明雷墩子年代较晚，或只是清代烽燧而已
note: an argument from preservation, not from finds

author: Huang Yinzhou et al.
asr_identification: the Shazhou–Yizhou road: Changting → Gancao → Xinjing → NE to near Guangxian (W of Baidunzi)
evidence: Huang traces the road of the Fifth Road from Shazhou: E to Gancao, then Xinjing, then NE to Guangxian; Baidunzi is generally taken for the Guangxian post.
quote: 再东北行抵达广显驿附近（白墩子西）
note: Bazhou No. 2 → Baidunzi → Hongliuyuan is 71 km for P.2005's 149 li to Wushan (0.48 km per li), within the road's range (route/p2005_posts.py)
